ELMALILI:13:7-11/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r15.claim: Secret speech and public speech, hiding by night and moving openly by day are all equally known to God.
ELMALILI:13:7-11/r15.anchor: içinizden sözünü gizleyen küfrü gönlünde söyleyen

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.claim: An unnamed man afflicted with a camel-like swelling returned to al-Sululiyya's home repeating his fate, died on horseback, and the passage about secret and public speech through disbelievers' prayer was revealed about him.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p273/r1.anchor: كغدة البعير، فعاد إلى بيت السلولية وهو يقول: غدة كغدة البعير وموت في بيت السلولية، ثم مات على ظهر فرسه

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Islahi rejects the codices' Madinan classification: in his view, the sūra is wholly Makkan, with no Madinan verse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Some codices regard it to be Madī nan, which I fail to understand. Not one of its verse is Mad īnan in my opinion

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God knows every deed and thought, whether secret or open and whether done by day or night.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: all their deeds and thoughts are in God’s knowledge whether done secretly or openly – in the light of the day or in the dark of the night.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Angels appointed by God watch over people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Angels deputed by God are overseeing them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God knows every hidden and open act by day and night, so no wrongdoer can escape His grasp or force Him to act hastily.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He knows what they conceal and reveal and every move they make in the day and night.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r6.claim: Sārib is an active participle of saraba and describes someone moving about freely as he wishes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r6.anchor: السارب: اسم فاعل من سرب أي تصرف كيف شاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r7.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r7.claim: An unnamed poet uses saribtu and sarūb to show the sense of moving freely.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r7.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
إني سربت وكنت غير سروب ... وتقرب الأحلام غير قريب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r8.speaker: الآخر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r8.claim: A second unnamed poet describes a camel freed from its tether as sārib, roaming without restraint.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p341/r8.anchor:
وقال الآخر:
وكل أناس قاربوا قيد فحلهم ... ونحن حللنا قيده فهو سارب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r14.claim: After describing God's knowledge of unseen and witnessed matters generally, the passage specifies His knowledge of the accountable person's hidden and spoken words.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p357/r14.anchor: ولما ذكر أنه تعالى عالم الغيب والشهادة على العموم، ذكر تعالى تعلق علمه بشيء خاص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses مستخف as concealed and سارب as visible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: مستخف مستتر وسارب ظاهر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r2.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r2.claim: Mujahid interprets مستخف as one who hides sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r2.anchor:
وقال مجاهد: مستخف بالمعاصي.
وتفسير الأخفش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r3.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r3.claim: Al-Akhfash and Qutrub take مستخف to mean visible, a possible lexical meaning that Abu Hayyan finds unsuitable beside night, in contrast to the daytime traveler.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r3.anchor: وتفسير الأخفش وقطرب: المستخفي هنا بالظاهر، وإن كان موجودا في اللغة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r4.claim: The paired descriptions correspond to the earlier pair: hidden at night matches secretly speaking, and moving openly by day matches speaking aloud; God's knowledge encompasses people's words and deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r4.anchor: وتقابل الوصفان في قوله: ومن هو مستخف، إذ قابل من أسر القول.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r5.claim: The apparent division requires repeating من before the second description; Basran grammarians disallow its omission, while Kufans allow it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r5.anchor: وظاهر التقسيم يقتضي تكرار من، لكنه حذف للعلم به، إذ تقدم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r6.claim: Alternatively, سارب may coordinate with من, making two contrasted people: one hidden at night and another traveling by day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r6.anchor:
ويجوز أن يكون:
وسارب، معطوفا على من، لا على مستخف، فيصح التقسيم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r7.claim: Another parsing coordinates سارب with مستخف and treats من as referring to two people by meaning; Ibn Atiyya describes this as one person whose conduct is consistently free of suspicion and equally known to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r7.anchor: وأريد بمن اثنان، وحمل على المعنى في تقسيم خبر المبتدأ الذي هو هو،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya says the lack of a repeated من supports a single category, since omission of من is found only in poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r8.anchor: ويؤيد هذا التأويل عطف السارب دون تكرار من، ولا يأتي حذفها إلا في الشعر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r9.claim: A third reading sees three classes: one who speaks secretly, an opposite person who speaks openly, and a changeable person who sins secretly at night but appears innocent by day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r9.anchor: وتحتمل الآية أن تتضمن ثلاثة أصناف. فالذي يسر طرف، والذي يجهر طرف مضاد للأول،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r10.claim: A hidden person may be concealing deeds in the darkness of night, as illustrated by two quoted poetic lines.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p358/r10.anchor: وقيل: ومن هو مستخف بالليل بظلمته، يريد إخفاء عمله فيه كما قال:

QASHANI:13:10-11/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:10-11/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:10-11/r1.claim: Secret speech remains latent, while public speech brings knowledge from potentiality into actuality.
QASHANI:13:10-11/r1.anchor: { سواء منكم من أسر القول } في مكمن استعداده { ومن جهر به } بإبراز العلم من القوة إلى الفعل

QASHANI:13:10-11/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:13:10-11/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:13:10-11/r2.claim: The hidden person is immersed in the self’s dark night, while the traveler leaves the self’s station for the spirit’s daylight.
QASHANI:13:10-11/r2.anchor: بليل ظلمة نفسه { و } من هو { سارب } بخروجه من مقام النفس وذهابه في نهار نور الروح

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r2.claim: God's knowledge treats private and public speech alike; the person concealed at night and the one moving visibly by day are equally known.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r2.anchor: {سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به} أي: يستوي في علم الله المسر بالقول والجاهر به،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r3.claim: Mستخف means covered by night's darkness; sārib means openly moving along a path by day.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r3.anchor: {ومن هو مستخف بالليل} أي: مستتر بظلمة الليل، {وسارب بالنهار} أي: ذاهب في سربه ظاهر.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r4.speaker: القتيبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r4.claim: Al-Qutaybī says the daytime traveler is occupied with his affairs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r4.anchor: قال القتيبي: سارب بالنهار: أي متصرف في حوائجه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a person who hides at night out of suspicion and appears by day as if innocent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس [في هذه الآية] (2) هو صاحب ريبة، مستخف بالليل، فإذا خرج بالنهار أرى الناس أنه بريء من الإثم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r6.claim: Another lexical view takes nighttime concealment as appearing, based on خفي meaning to reveal; the daytime traveler is then hidden inside a passage.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p299/r6.anchor: وقيل: مستخف بالليل، أي: ظاهر، من قولهم: خفيت الشيء؛ إذا أظهرته، وأخفيته: إذا كتمته.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.claim: Al-Raʿd’s aim is to portray revelation as true in itself: sometimes its sound and fame move people toward guidance, while sometimes it instead leaves them blind and astray, like thunder whose lightning and rain may benefit, fail, or harm according to where they fall.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p116#s013/r1.anchor: مقصودها وصف الكتاب بأنه الحق في نفسه ، وتارة يتأثر عنه مع أن له صوتا وصيتا وإرعابا وإرهابا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r1.claim: Because people differ in how much they know of secrets and how much power guards provide, the passage explains that hidden and open matters are equal to God’s knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r1.anchor: أتبع ذلك سبحانه بما نفي هذا الاحتمال عنه على وجه الشرح والبيان لاستواء الغيب والشهادة بالنسبة إلى علمه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r2.claim: God’s knowledge is equal regarding whoever conceals speech and whoever declares it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r2.anchor: سواء منكم } أي في علمه { من أسر القول } أي أخفى معناه في نفسه { ومن جهر به

BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r3.claim: Mustakhfin is one who actively seeks concealment, especially at night, believing that hiding can keep divine power from reaching him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r3.anchor: مستخف } أي موجد الخفاء وطالب له أشد طلب { باليل } في أخفى الأوقات

BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r4.claim: Sārib is someone moving quickly toward his purpose across the earth in daylight, openly traversing it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r4.anchor: سارب } أي ذاهب على وجهه الأرض ومتوجه جار في توجهه إلى قصده بسرعة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r5.claim: The verse uses iḥtibāk: mentioning the concealed one first implies his counterpart later, and mentioning the traveler later implies his counterpart earlier.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p130/r5.anchor: ذكر { مستخف } أولا دال على ضده ثانيا

DURR-FULL:v4p616/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p616/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p616/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that Amir ibn al-Tufayl demanded power and territory from the Prophet, threatened to muster against him after refusal, and conspired with Arbad to assassinate him; Arbad could not draw his sword when God's protection intervened.
DURR-FULL:v4p616/r3.anchor: عن ابن زيد - رضي الله عنه - قال: أتى عامر بن الطفيل وأربد بن ربيعة إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال له عامر

DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.claim: The report concludes that lightning killed Arbad and plague killed Amir; Ibn Zayd links their story to the verses on hidden and spoken words, protecting angels, and the futility of disbelievers' prayers.
DURR-FULL:v4p617/r1.anchor: فخرج أربد حتى إذا كان بالرقم بعث الله سحابة من الصيف فيها صاعقة فأحرقته وخرج عامر حتى إذا كان بوادي الحريد أرسل الله عليه الطاعون

AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r1.claim: مستخف بالليل means apparent, while سارب بالنهار means concealed.
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r1.anchor: وقال {مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار} فقوله {مستخف} يقول: ظاهر. و"السارب": المتواري.

AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r2.claim: A reading أخفيها can mean I reveal it, since Arabic خفيت السر can mean I disclosed the secret.
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r2.anchor: وقد قرئت (أخفيها) أي: أظهرها لأنك تقول "خفيت السر" أي: أظهرته

AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r3.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r3.claim: An unidentified mutaqārib poem uses نخفه to mean reveal it, supporting the cited usage of خفيت.
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r3.anchor: إن تكتموا الداء لا نخفه * وإن تبعثوا الحرب لا نقعد

AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r4.claim: Akhfash says the reading with ḍamma is better.

AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r5.speaker: زعموا
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r5.claim: Some claim أكاد means أريد as a dialectal usage; أريد can replace أكاد, as جدارا يريد أن ينقض means it is about to collapse.
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r5.anchor: وزعموا أن تفسير (أكاد) : أريد وأنها لغة لأن "أريد" قد تجعل مكان "أكاد" مثل (جدارا يريد ان ينقض)

AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r6.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r6.claim: An unidentified kāmil poet's كادت وكدت and خير إرادة is cited as evidence for the relation between أكاد and إرادة.
AKHFASH:v2p402#2/r6.anchor: كادت وكدت وتلك خير إرادة * لو عاد من لهو الصبابة ما مضى

FARRA:v2p59/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p59/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p59/r1.claim: Both occurrences of من are nominative because سواء governs them: whoever speaks secretly or openly, God knows him; it also means the visible and hidden are equal to Him.
FARRA:v2p59/r1.anchor: الذي رفعهما جميعا سواء، ومعناهما: أن من أسر القول أو جهر به

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r1.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r1.claim: Sawāʾ stands for mustawٍ; the sense is that the one who conceals speech and the one who declares it are alike to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r1.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري ناب سواء عن مستو والمعنى مستو منكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r2.claim: The one hidden and the one publicly active are equally known to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r2.anchor: والمعنى أن السر والجهر سواء عنده

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r3.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r3.claim: Most exegetes take the one hidden at night as concealed in darkness and the sārir by day as visible and moving about; the phrase means visible and hidden are alike to God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r3.anchor: أن المستخفي هو المستتر المتواري في ظلمة الليل والسارب بالنهار الظاهر المتصرف في حوائجة يقال سربت الإبل تسرب إذا مضت في الأرض ظاهرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r4.claim: A line of poetry uses sārir for one who goes away and supports this gloss.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r4.anchor: وأنشدوا أرى كل قوم قاربوا قيد فحلهم ونحن خلعنا قيده فهو سارب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r5.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r5.claim: The hidden person is a suspicious person by night who presents himself as innocent when he emerges in daylight.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r5.anchor: وروى العوفي عن ابن عباس ومن هو مستخف قال صاحب ريبة بالليل فإذا خرج بالنهار أرى الناس أنه بريء من الإثم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r6.speaker: الأخفش، قطرب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r6.claim: An opposing view makes the one hidden at night apparent and the one moving by day concealed; انسرب means an animal entered its den.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r6.anchor: أن المستخفي بالليل الظاهر والسارب بالنهار المستتر يقال انسرب الوحش إذا دخل في كناسه وهذا قول الأخفش وذكره قطرب أيضا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r7.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r7.claim: Ibn Jarīr supports the opposing reading from the usage خفيت الشيء meaning “I revealed it,” as in 20:15; sārir is named for hiding in a burrow.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p309/r7.anchor: واحتج له ابن جرير بقولهم خفيت الشيء إذا أظهرته ومنه ( أكاد أخفيها ) [ طه 15 ] بفتح الألف أي أظهرها

MAJAZ:v1p322/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p322/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p322/r8.claim: Sārib means one travelling through his routes and directions; being safe in one's sarb means safe wherever one turns.
MAJAZ:v1p322/r8.anchor: مجازه: سالك فى سربه، أي مذاهبه ووجوهه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r1.claim: God's knowledge encompasses everyone, whether they conceal or voice their words; He hears all and nothing escapes Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r1.anchor: يخبر تعالى عن إحاطة علمه بجميع خلقه، سواء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r2.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r2.claim: Aisha says a woman came to plead about her husband while Aisha was beside the house and could not hear some of their conversation; God then revealed that He had heard their exchange.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r2.anchor: وقالت عائشة، رضي الله عنها: سبحان الذي وسع سمعه الأصوات، والله لقد جاءت المجادلة تشتكي زوجها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r3.claim: One hidden in a house at night and one walking openly in daylight are equally within God's knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p437/r3.anchor: ومن هو مستخف بالليل} أي: مختف في قعر بيته في ظلام الليل، {وسارب بالنهار} أي: ظاهر ماش

NAHHAS:v2p353/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p353/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v2p353/r1.claim: Sawāʾ is nominative because its predicate is understood as delayed.
NAHHAS:v2p353/r1.anchor: مرفوع ينوى به التأخير قال أبو إسحاق والتقدير

NAHHAS:v2p353/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p353/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v2p353/r2.claim: Abū Isḥāq estimates dhawū sawāʾ, as in rajul ʿadl; he also proposes sawāʾ means equal, a nominative subject, though he says Sibawayh disallows beginning with an indefinite.
NAHHAS:v2p353/r2.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق والتقدير ذو سواء كما يقال رجل عدل وقيل سواء بمعنى مستو وهو مرفوع بالابتداء

NAHHAS:v2p353/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p353/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
NAHHAS:v2p353/r3.claim: The meaning is that these people are equal before God and His knowledge of them is the same.
NAHHAS:v2p353/r3.anchor: قال أبو جعفر والمعنى أنه يستوي عند الله جل وعز هؤلاء وعلمه بهم واحد

NAHHAS:v2p353/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p353/r4.speaker: حسان
NAHHAS:v2p353/r4.claim: Ḥassān's poem uses sawāʾ to mean equal in standing before God, whether people insult, praise, or defend the Messenger.
NAHHAS:v2p353/r4.anchor:
وقال حسان
( فمن يهجو رسول الله منكم

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r1.claim: Secret speech is what a person says to himself; open speech is what he says to another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r1.anchor: إسرار القول : ما حدث به نفسه , والجهر ما حدث به غيره .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r2.claim: God knows whatever a person conceals, whether good or evil.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r2.anchor: والمراد بذلك أنه تعالى يعلم ما أسره الإنسان من خير وشر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r3.claim: One reading is that God knows the one who hides his deeds in night and the one who appears by day.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r3.anchor: أحدهما : يعلم من استخفى بعمله في ظلمة الليل , ومن أظهره في ضوء النهار .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r4.claim: Alternatively, God sees what night hides as clearly as what daylight shows, unlike human beings who cannot see their families' nighttime states.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r4.anchor: الثاني : يرى ما أخفته ظلمة الليل كما يرى ما أظهره ضوء النهار , بخلاف المخلوقين الذين يخفي عليهم الليل أحوال أهلهم .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r5.claim: An unnamed poet illustrates that clear-sighted and impaired eyes alike are equal in the darkness of night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r5.anchor: قال الشاعر : وليل يقول الناس في ظلماته … سواء صحيحات العيون وعورها

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r6.claim: Al-sārib is one who departs or goes away, from the term for grazing movement; sarūb is used of evening, sarūj of morning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r6.anchor: والسارب : هو المنصرف الذاهب , مأخوذ من السروب في المرعى , وهو بالعشي , والسروج بالغداة , قال قيس بن الخطيم :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r7.speaker: قيس بن الخطيم
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r7.claim: Qays ibn al-Khatim's line uses sarabt to illustrate the term for departing or going away.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p97/r7.anchor: قال قيس بن الخطيم : أنى سربت وكنت غير سروب … وتقرب الأحلام غير قريب

MUQATIL:13:10-11/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:13:10-11/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:13:10-11/r1.claim: God regards secret and public speech equally; the person hidden in sin at night spreads that same sin openly by day, and God knows it all.
MUQATIL:13:10-11/r1.anchor: يقول: من هو مستخف بالمعصية في ظلمة الليل، ومنتشر بتلك المعصية بالنهار معلن بها

TAB-FULL:v13p471/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p471/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p471/r4.claim: He paraphrases the passage as describing people who conceal sin at night and move openly by day, relying on guards to prevent God's followers from enforcing His limits.
TAB-FULL:v13p471/r4.anchor: ومن هو مستخف بفسقه وريبته في ظلمة الليل، وسارب: يذهب ويجيء في ضوء النهار

TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r3.claim: A Basran grammarian reads mukhfi as manifest at night, from a verb meaning to reveal, and takes sari as hidden during the day.
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r3.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي أهل البصرة: معنى قوله: {ومن هو مستخف بالليل} [الرعد: 10] ومن هو ظاهر بالليل، من قولهم: خفيت الشيء: إذا أظهرته

TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r4.speaker: امرؤ القيس
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r4.claim: The Basran grammarian cites Imruʾ al-Qays's verb nukhfihi (“we reveal it”) as evidence for khafiya meaning to make manifest.
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r4.anchor: وكما قال امرؤ القيس: [البحر الوافر] فإن تكتموا الداء لا نخفه

TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r5.speaker: بعض نحويي أهل البصرة
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r5.claim: The Basran cites the reading “I almost reveal it” as another instance of akhfi meaning “make manifest.”

TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r6.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة والكوفة
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r6.claim: Other Basran and Kufan grammarians read mukhfi as concealed and sari as going out by day, from camels going to pasture; another usage distinguishes evening movement from morning departure.
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي البصرة والكوفة: إنما معنى ذلك: ومن هو مستخف: أي مستتر بالليل من الاستخفاء، وسارب بالنهار: وذاهب بالنهار

TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī allows that the Basran grammatical reading has an Arabic basis but rejects it because it conflicts with all the reported exegetes.
TAB-FULL:v13p471#2/r9.anchor: وأما الذي ذكرناه عن نحويي البصريين في ذلك فقول وإن كان له في كلام العرب وجه خلاف لقول أهل التأويل

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r1.claim: Both occurrences of man are nominative through sawāʾ, which requires two parties, as in saying Zayd and ʿAmr are equal.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r1.anchor: رفع بسواء، وكذلك (من) الثانية يرتفعان جميعا بسواء، لأن

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r2.claim: Because sawāʾ is a verbal noun, the following nouns are raised by ellipsis: the sense is ‘possessors of equality’; verbal nouns do not directly raise nouns as participles do.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r2.anchor: لأن سواء مصدر فلا يجوز أن يرتفع ما بعده إلا على الحذف،

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r3.speaker: الخنساء
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r3.claim: Al-Khansāʾ’s line illustrates the omitted possessive noun: in reality she is possessed of coming and going.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r3.anchor: كما قالت الخنساء: ترتع ما غفلت حتى إذا ادكرت. . . فإنما هي إقبال وإدبار

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r4.claim: The construction is so common with sawāʾ that it has come to behave like an active participle.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r4.anchor: وهذا مما كثر استعماله أعني سواء، فجرى مجرى أسماء الفاعلين

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r5.claim: A second analysis treats the nominative as a predicate meaning ‘equal’; Sibawayh considers this poor because indefinite active participles are too weak to begin a clause, treating them like verbs.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r5.anchor: في موضع مستو، إلا أن سيبويه يستقبح ذلك،

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r6.claim: The verse declares that God knows what is hidden and what is witnessed.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r6.anchor: ومعنى الآية إعلامهم أن الله عز وجل يعلم ما غاب عنهم وما شهد.

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r7.claim: Mustakhfin by night means concealed, since night conceals more than day.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r7.anchor: أي من هو مستتر بالليل، والليل أستر من النهار

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r8.claim: Sārib by day means visible on his route; sarb means a path, as in ‘leave his sarb open.’
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r8.anchor: أي من هو ظاهر بالنهار في سربه، يقال: خل له سربه أي طريقه،

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r9.claim: God knows equally those who speak aloud and those who conceal their words in themselves.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r9.anchor: والجاهر بنطقه والمضمر في نفسه علم الله فيهم جميعا سواء

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r10.speaker: قطرب
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r10.claim: Qutrub allows mustakhfin by night to mean visible and sārib by day to mean hidden, as when a wild animal enters its lair.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r10.anchor: وذكر قطرب وجها آخر، ذكر أنه يجوز أن يكون " مستخف بالليل "

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r11.claim: The expression انسرب الوحشي means the wild animal entered its lair.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r11.anchor: يقال: انسرب الوحشي إذا دخل في كناسه.

ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r12.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r12.claim: The first interpretation is clear and more powerful in depicting God’s knowledge of the unseen.
ZAJJAJ:v3p141/r12.anchor: والأول بين، وهو أبلغ في وصف علم الغيب.

TABRISI:13:8-11/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-11/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-11/r12.claim: “Al-sārib” can mean a swift traveler, a stream of water from a waterskin, or one who goes across the land; Dhu al-Rumma's verse witnesses the flowing-water sense, and Qays b. al-Khatim's the traveling sense.
TABRISI:13:8-11/r12.anchor: والسارب الساري الجاري بسرعة والسرب بفتح السين والراء الماء السائل من المزادة قال ذو الرمة

TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r1.claim: A quoted line uses “sarabtu” for going out or roaming across the earth; the proverb “leave his sarb” means leave his way free.

TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r6.claim: In “equal are you,” both “whoever conceals” and “whoever speaks openly” are nominative because “equal” calls for two terms; it means “having equality,” with an omitted possessive complement.
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به موضع من رفع بسواء وكذلك من الثانية يرتفعان جميعا بسواء لأن سواء يطلب اثنين

TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r7.claim: Because “sawāʾ” is a verbal noun rather than an active adjective, its following nouns are raised only by ellipsis, as if saying “possessing equality.”
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r7.anchor: لأن سواء مصدر فلا يجوز أن يرتفع ما بعده إلا على الحذف تقول عدل زيد وعمرو والمعنى ذو عدل زيد وعمرو

TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r8.claim: A quoted line says the subject is only coming and going, illustrating nominal predicates construed with an omitted possessive expression.
TABRISI:13:8-11#2/r8.anchor: ترتع ما رتعت حتى إذا ادكرت

TABRISI:13:11/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:11/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:11/r1.claim: God sees what night conceals just as He sees what daylight reveals, unlike creatures whose knowledge of people's affairs is obscured by night.
TABRISI:13:11/r1.anchor: معناه أنه يرى ما أخفته ظلمة الليل كما يرى ما أظهره ضوء النهار بخلاف المخلوقين الذين يخفي عليهم الليل أحوال أهله

TABRISI:13:11/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:11/r2.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:13:11/r2.claim: Al-Hasan interprets the phrase as whoever is concealed at night and whoever is concealed by day; al-Zajjaj approves because Arabic describes an animal entering its den as “انسرب الوحش.”
TABRISI:13:11/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن معناه ومن هو مستتر بالليل ومن هو مستتر بالنهار وصحح الزجاج هذا القول لأن العرب تقول انسرب الوحش

THALABI:v5p278/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p278/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p278/r1.claim: The account connects the episode of ʿAmir and Arbad to the passage beginning “whether one conceals speech.”
THALABI:v5p278/r1.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى في هذه القصة سواء منكم من أسر القول الآية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r2.claim: God equally knows the openly speaking and inwardly concealing person, and the visible and hidden one; hidden means concealed and sārib means apparent and moving along.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:13:9-11/r2.anchor: علم الله سبحانه فيهم جميعا سواء، والمستخفي معناه: المختفي، والسارب: الظاهر المار على وجهه

SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r1.claim: On one parse سواء is a fronted predicate and من أسر with ومن جهر the subject; it stays singular because it is originally a verbal noun meaning equal, while منكم is circumstantial to its implicit subject.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { سواء منكم من أسر }: في " سواء " وجهان، أحدهما: أنه خبر مقدم، و { من أسر }

SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa rejects taking منكم as circumstantial to the hidden subject of أسر or جهر: that would front material from the relative clause and place the predicate before منكم.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r2.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ويضعف أن يكون حالا من الضمير في " أسر " أو " جهر " لوجهين

SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r3.claim: Alternatively سواء is a subject, allowed because it is qualified by منكم; Sibawayh parses سواء عليه الخير والشر likewise. Ibn Atiyya wrongly claims Sibawayh weakened this parse as an indefinite subject.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه مبتدأ، وجاز الابتداء به لوصفه بقوله " منكم " وأعرب سيبويه " سواء عليه الخير والشر "

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r1.claim: One analysis coordinates سارب with مستخف; من denotes two people, while هو remains singular by form and the predicate follows the dual sense.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن يكون معطوفا على " مستخف " ، ويراد ب " من " حينئذ اثنان

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r2.claim: A second analysis coordinates سارب with من هو مستخف as a whole, yielding a parallel of one hidden by night and another roaming by day.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r2.anchor: أن قوله " وسارب " عطف على { من هو مستخف } لا على " مستخف ".

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r3.claim: A third possibility deletes the relative من before هو سارب; al-Samin says this works only for Kufan grammarians, who permit omission of a relative pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r3.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون على حذف " من " الموصولة، أي: ومن هو سارب، وهذا إنما يتمشى عند الكوفيين

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid hold that one person is meant: he hides at night and roams by day, allowing people to observe his dealings.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r4.anchor: وهو مذهب ابن عباس ومجاهد، ذهبا إلى أن المتسخفي والسارب شخص واحد، يستخفي بالليل

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r5.claim: سارب is the active participle of سرب, to roam at will; the cited wolf poem uses يصطحبان to show singular من referring to two by sense.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r5.anchor: والسارب: اسم فاعل من سرب يسرب، أي: تصرف كيف شاء.

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r6.claim: Al-Samin says the wolf poem coordinates on sense alone, not both form and sense, and criticizes al-Zamakhshari’s claim that the wording ought to differ as bad manners.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r6.anchor: وليس في البيت حمل على اللفظ والمعنى، إنما فيه حمل على المعنى فقط، وهو مقصوده.

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r7.claim: An anonymous poet uses سربت for going about, in أنى سربت وكنت غير سروب.

SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r8.claim: Another poet calls his unrestrained people سارب: they released their fettered camel and roam freely, boasting of strength and protection.
SAMIN-DURR:13:10#2/r8.anchor: وقال آخر: 2845- وكل أناس قاربوا قيد فحلهم

ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n22/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n22/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n22/r1.claim: Qawl primarily means a saying or utterance, but can figuratively mean an idea whether spoken or merely conceived; here it means unspoken thoughts.
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n22/r1.anchor: Since in the above verse this term obviously refers to unspoken thoughts, I have rendered it accordingly.

ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r1.speaker: Ibn 'Abbas
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by Baghawi and Razi, interprets going forth by day as committing evil deeds openly.
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r1.anchor: commits evil deeds openly (Ibn 'Abbas, as quoted by Baghawi and Razi)

ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r2.claim: The Arabic syntax sets concealed thought and openly expressed thought alongside the person hidden by night and the one moving by day, all equally known to God.
ASAD-NOTES:13:10#n23/r2.anchor: In the Arabic construction, the sentence reads thus

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p332#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p332#3/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p332#3/r1.claim: Al-Hasan and Qatada gloss the one moving openly by day as visible and going about.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p332#3/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن الحسن وقتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وسارب بالنهار ﴾ قالا ظاهر ذاهب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r1.claim: One who conceals speech may keep it within himself without uttering it, or utter it so quietly that only he hears it.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r1.anchor: أخفاه في نفسه ولم يتلفظ به وقيل : تلفظ به بحيث لم يسمع نفسه دون غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r2.claim: The glosses of public speech correspond to those two senses of concealed speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r2.anchor: ومن جهر به ( من يقابل ذلك بالمعنيين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r3.claim: Mustakhfin describes someone hiding intensely, as if wholly concealed.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r3.anchor: مبالغ في الاخفاء كأنه مختف ( بالليل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the daytime sārib as one who goes about openly or freely; that sense is implied by its contrast with one concealed at night.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r4.anchor: أي ظافر فيه كما روى عن ابن عباس وهو ما قال جمع في الأصل اسم فاعل

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r5.claim: Sārib is the active participle of saraba, to go along one’s way, and can mean moving about as one wishes.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r5.anchor: اسم فاعل من سرب إذا ذهب في سربه أي طريقه ويكون بمعنى تصرف كيف شاء

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r6.speaker: الشاعر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r6.claim: The first poem uses sarabtu for going forth, supporting the root sense of sārib.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر : إني سربت وكنت غير سروب وتقرب الأحلام غير قريب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r7.speaker: الآخر
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r7.claim: The second poem uses sārib for someone moving freely, unrestrained by the grazing rope.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r7.anchor: وقال الآخر : وكل أناس قاربوا قيد فحلهم ونحن خلعنا قيده فهو سارب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r8.claim: Some take sārib literally as visible; Ibn ʿAbbās’s gloss instead gives its implication, supported by its contrast with mustakhfin.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r8.anchor: فما ذكره الحبر لازم معناه وقرينته وقوعه في مقابلة مستخف

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r9.claim: Sawāʾ is a fronted predicate and man the delayed subject; the predicate is not normally dualized because it began as a verbal noun, though Abū Zayd reports “they are two equals.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r9.anchor: ورفع ( سواء ) على أنه خبر مقدم و ( من ) مبتدأ مؤخر ولم يثن الخبر لأنه في الأصل مصدر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r10.claim: Min-kum is circumstantial of the implied subject within sawāʾ, not of asarra or jahara, since a relative-clause element cannot precede its antecedent.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r10.anchor: و ( منكم ) حال من الضمير المستتر فيه لافي ( أسر ) و ( جهر ) لأن مافي حيز الصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r11.claim: Abū Ḥayyān allows sawāʾ as the subject, described by min-kum, with what follows as predicate, as in Sibawayh’s Arabic example “good and evil are equal to him.”
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r11.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان كون ( سواء ) مبتدأ لوصفه بمنكم وما بعده الخبر وكذا أعرب سيبويه قول العرب

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r12.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says Sibawayh weakened the parse because it begins with an indefinite, which he considered invalid.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r12.anchor: وقول ابن عطية : إن سيبويه ضعف ذلك بأنه ابتداء بنكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r13.claim: Sārib coordinates with man, meaning another person; adding huwa with mustakhfin confirms the complete knowledge of God, while the description is omitted before sārib.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r13.anchor: كأنه قيل : سواء منكم إنسان هو مستخف وآخر سارب والنكتة في زيادة هو

ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r14.claim: Because sawāʾ requires two compared things, a difficulty arises if sārib attaches within the description; the response is that man can denote two, as in a cited verse about a wolf and its companion.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p110#2/r14.anchor: واستشكل بأن سواء يقتضي ذكر شيئين فإذا كان سارب معطوفا على جزء الصلة

ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r1.speaker: صاحب الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r1.claim: For the generic reading, the relative and descriptive constructions mean the same, but the descriptive form is more explicit; a definite referent would suggest an unintended implication.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r1.anchor: فهو والأول سواء لكن الأول نص وإن أريد المعهود حقيقة أو تقديرا لزم ايهام خلاف المقصود لما مر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r2.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r2.claim: Some posit an omitted relative pronoun, expanding the phrase to “and one who is going freely,” as in poems by Abū Firās and Ḥassān.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r2.anchor: كقول أبي فراس : فليت الذي بيني وبينك عامر وبيني وبين العالمين خراب وقول حسان

ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows either of the two omissions individually but calls their combination unacceptable; Abū Ḥayyān says Basrans forbid this deletion while Kufans allow it.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r3.anchor: وقد ادعى الزمخشري أن أحد الحذفين سائغ لكن اجتماعهما منكر من المنكرات بخلاف البيتين

ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r4.claim: Some say the verse compares states of concealment at night and free movement by day in God’s knowledge, whether one person or two; al-Ālūsī objects that Arabic syntax does not support this nominalized reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r4.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن المقصود استواء الحالتين سواء كانتا لواحد أو لاثنين والمعنى سواء استخفاؤه وسرو به

ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya proposes three classes: a secret speaker, an outspoken opposite, and a person who sins secretly at night but feigns innocence by day; al-Ālūsī dismisses this.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r5.anchor: وزعم ابن عطية جواز أن تكون الآية متضمنة ثلاثة أصناف فالذي يسر طرف والذي يجهر طرف مضاد للأول

ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r6.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash and Quṭrub reportedly gloss mustakhfin as visible; although that sense exists in Arabic, al-Ālūsī says the verse’s context rules it out.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r6.anchor: ومن الغريب مانقل عن الأخفش وقطرب تفسير المستخفى بالظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r7.claim: After establishing that God’s knowledge encompasses everything, the further enumeration signals special attention to these cases.
ALUSI-FULL:v13p111/r7.anchor: ثم أن في بيان علمه تعالى بماذكر بعد بيان شمول علمه سبحانه الاشياء كلها

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r1.claim: One who conceals speech keeps it within himself; one who makes it public speaks to another.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r1.anchor: { سواء منكم من أسر القول } في نفسه. { ومن جهر به } لغيره.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r2.claim: The one hidden at night seeks concealment in a nighttime hiding place.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r2.anchor: { ومن هو مستخف بالليل } طالب للخفاء في مختبأ بالليل.

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r3.claim: Sārib means appearing openly by day, from saraba, to emerge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r3.anchor: { وسارب } بارز. { بالنهار } يراه كل أحد من سرب سروبا إذا برز

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r4.claim: Sārib may coordinate with man or mustakhfin, treating man as dual, as in the cited line where two companions are meant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r4.anchor: وهو عطف على من أو مستخف على أن من في معنى الإثنين كقوله:

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r5.speaker: الشاعر
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r5.claim: The cited line uses man to mean two people, supporting the dual construction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r5.anchor: نكن مثل من يا ذئب يصطحبان

BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r6.claim: The verse connects to the preceding description and confirms God’s complete and comprehensive knowledge.
BAYDAWI-FULL:13:10/r6.anchor: والآية متصلة بما قبلها مقررة لكمال علمه وشموله

BURSEVI:v4p229/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p229/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p229/r1.claim: Sawāʾ is the predicate of man; minkum is a circumstantial phrase referring to it because it means equal. It remains singular because it is originally a verbal noun, though equality entails two persons.

BURSEVI:v4p229/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p229/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p229/r2.claim: God's knowledge equally encompasses whoever keeps speech inward and whoever voices it aloud.
BURSEVI:v4p229/r2.anchor: والمعنى مستو في علم الله تعالى من أضمر القول في نفسه

BURSEVI:v4p229/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p229/r3.speaker: بحر العلوم
BURSEVI:v4p229/r3.claim: Sārib is coordinated with man, yielding two people: one concealed in darkness and another visible along the roads, as Bahr al-ʿUlūm explains.
BURSEVI:v4p229/r3.anchor: وسارب معطوف على من فيتحقق شيآن ومن موصوفة كأنه قيل سواء منكم إنسان هو مستتر ومتوار في الظلمات وآخر ظاهر في الطرقات كما قال في بحر العلوم

BURSEVI:v4p229/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p229/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v4p229/r4.claim: The lexicons gloss istikhfāʾ as becoming hidden, sarab as going by day, and sarb as a road; sārib is someone going along his route openly in daylight, visible to everyone.
BURSEVI:v4p229/r4.anchor: والسرب بفتح السين وسكون الراء الطريق كما في القاموس

BURSEVI:v4p229/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v4p229/r5.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v4p229/r5.claim: Al-Kāshifī says people who hide their actions at night and disclose them by day cannot conceal anything, in speech or deed, secret or public.

DURR-FULL:v4p610/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r4.claim: Mujahid says God knows secret and public speech equally; the hidden night sinner and the open daytime sinner are equally known.
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به} قال: من أسره وأعلنه عنده سواء

DURR-FULL:v4p610/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r5.claim: Qatada says secret is as public and darkness as light before God.
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r5.anchor: عن قتادة - رضي الله عنه - {سواء منكم

DURR-FULL:v4p610/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r6.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says God knows secrecy as publicity, and night as day, in both directions.
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r6.anchor: عن الحسن - رضي الله عنه - في الآية قال: يعلم من السر ما يعلم من العلانية ويعلم من العلانية ما يعلم من السر

DURR-FULL:v4p610/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas defines sāʾib by day as someone visible.
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {وسارب بالنهار} قال: الظاهر

DURR-FULL:v4p610/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas identifies the night-hidden, day-visible person as someone under suspicion who presents himself as innocent.
DURR-FULL:v4p610/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - في قوله {ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار} قال: هو صاحب ريبة

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the verse was revealed concerning Amir and Arbad and their intentions toward the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ، عن ابن عباس قال : انزل الله تبارك وتعالى في عامر واربد وما كانا هما به من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : سواء منكم من اسر القول

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r2.claim: God knows what is secret as He knows what is public, and what is public as He knows what is secret.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن : سواء منكم من اسر القول أو جهر به قال : يعلم من السر ما يعلم من العلانية ، ويعلم من العلانية ما يعلم من السر

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r3.claim: All are alike before God: secret and public speech, darkness and light.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : سواء منكم من اسر القول ومن جهر به كل ذلك سواء عنده السر عنده علانية والظلمة عنده ضوء

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r4.claim: God knows what occurs at night as He knows what occurs by day, and vice versa.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r4.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : ومن هو مستخف بالليل قال : يعلم من الليل ما يعلم من النهار ، ويعلم من النهار ما يعلم من الليل

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r5.claim: Mujahid describes the person hidden at night as someone riding headlong in acts of disobedience.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : ومن هو مستخف بالليل قال : راكب راسه بالمعاصي

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r6.claim: Qatada says the person is concealed in the darkness of night.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة : ومن هو مستخف بالليل : اي في ظلمة الليل

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r7.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says saari b is one who goes about openly in the daytime.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r7.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول في قوله : مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار والسارب النادي بالنهار

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says the person goes out by day, appearing to people as though free of sin.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2228#2/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قوله : وسارب بالنهار : قال اذا خرج بالنهار ارى الناس انه بريء من الاثم

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports again that the verse was revealed concerning Amir and Arbad and what they had intended regarding the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r1.anchor: عن عطاء بن يسار ، عن ابن عباس قال : انزل الله تعالى في عامر واربد ما كانا هما به من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r2.claim: Mujahid says the person goes about openly committing sins by day.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2229/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد وسارب بالنهار قال : ظاهر بالنهار بالمعاصي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r1.claim: The sentence is an explanatory resumption and consequence of God’s comprehensive knowledge of hidden and manifest things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r1.anchor: موقع هذه الجملة استئناف بياني لأن مضمونها بمنزلة النتيجة لعموم علم الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r2.claim: The discourse shifts from third-person reference to direct address to teach both believers and unbelievers, while implicitly threatening polytheists conspiring against the Prophet.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r2.anchor: وعدل عن الغيبة المتبعة في الضمائر فيما تقدم إلى الخطاب هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r3.claim: Sawāʾ means equal and is used between two or more things; Arabic usage keeps it in one form, as in ‘they are equal’ and ‘you are equal in it.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r3.anchor: و { سواء } اسم بمعنى مستو . وإنما يقع معناه بين شيئين فصاعدا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r4.claim: One parse makes sawāʾ the subject and man the subject-like element filling the predicate slot; alternatively sawāʾ is a fronted predicate, man the delayed subject, and minkum a circumstantial phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r4.anchor: وموقع سواء هنا موقع المبتدأ . و { من أسر القول } فاعل سد مسد الخبر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r5.claim: Istikhfāʾ here means concealment; the sīn and tāʾ intensify the action, as in istajāba.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r5.anchor: والاستخفاء : هنا الخفاء ، فالسين والتاء للمبالغة في الفعل مثل استجاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r6.claim: Sārib is an active participle from saraba, to go along a road or path; this verb is derived from a concrete noun.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r6.anchor: والسارب : اسم فاعل من سرب إذا ذهب في السرب بفتح السين وسكون الراء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r7.claim: Concealment is paired with night because it is the more hidden state, and movement with day because it is more visible; both kinds are equally known to God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r7.anchor: وذكر الاستخفاء مع الليل لكونه أشد خفاء ، وذكر السروب مع النهار لكونه أشد ظهورا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r8.claim: The wāw joining the relative expressions marks division among the categories and therefore functions like ‘or.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p99/r8.anchor: والواو التي عطفت أسماء الموصول على الموصول الأول للتقسيم فهي بمعنى { أو }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabi rejects reconciling philosophical sciences with Qur’anic meanings because philosophy is mixed with doctrinal error; Ibn ʿĀshūr says he overdoes his contempt for philosophers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r1.anchor: وذهب ابن العربي في العواصم إلى إنكار التوفيق بين العلوم الفلسفية والمعاني القرآنية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r2.claim: The first level comprises sciences contained in the Qur’an: prophetic histories, ethics, jurisprudence, law, creed, legal theory, Arabic, and rhetoric.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r2.anchor: الأولى : علوم تضمنها القرآن كأخبار الأنبياء والأمم ، وتهذيب الأخلاق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r3.claim: The second level consists of fields that broaden an exegete’s knowledge, including wisdom, astronomy, and the properties of created things.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r3.anchor: الثانية : علوم تزيد المفسر علما كالحكمة والهيأة وخواص المخلوقات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r4.claim: The third level includes sciences to which the Qur’an alludes or which support it, such as earth strata, medicine, and logic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r4.anchor: الثالثة : علوم أشار إليها أو جاءت مؤيدة له كعلم طبقات الأرض والطب والمنطق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r5.claim: The fourth level comprises subjects unrelated to Qur’anic service: invalid arts like divination, augury, and mythology, or fields such as prosody and rhyme that do not assist interpretation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p45/r5.anchor: الرابعة : علوم لا علاقة لها به إما لبطلانها كالزجر والعيافة والميثولوجيا ، وإما لأنها لا تعين على خدمته كعلم العروض والقوافي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r1.claim: Sawāʾ is a verbal noun requiring two things to be compared; as a predicate of man it needs an implicit noun, as in the description “possessing approach and withdrawal.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r1.anchor: سواء مصدر وهو يطلب بعده شيئين يتماثلان. ورفعه على خبر الابتداء الذي هو «من» والمصدر لا يكون خبرا إلا بإضمار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r2.claim: One group supplies an implicit dhū, understanding the phrase as “possessing equality.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r2.anchor: فقالت فرقة هنا: المعنى: ذو سواء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj says frequent use made sawāʾ function like an active participle, so no implicit noun is needed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج كثر استعمال سواء في كلام العرب حتى جرى مجرى اسم الفاعل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya compares sawāʾ to ʿadl, zawr, and ḍayf, which likewise function as descriptions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r4.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: هو عندي كعدل وزور وضيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r5.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r5.claim: Another group reads the phrase as “equal among you”; Sībawayh objects that this begins with an indefinite noun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r5.anchor: وقالت فرقة: المعنى: مستو منكم، فلا يحتاج إلى إضمار. قال القاضي أبو محمد: وضعف هذا سيبويه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r6.claim: Those who whisper within themselves and those who speak aloud are equally encompassed by God's knowledge; nothing escapes Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r6.anchor: ومعنى هذه الآية: معتدل منكم في إحاطة الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r7.claim: Mustakhfin by night is completely concealed; sārin by day is someone moving about and going on his way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r7.anchor: من هو بالليل في غاية الاختفاء، ومن هو متصرف بالنهار ذاهب لوجهه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid understand the concealed person and daytime traveler as one suspicious man who hides at night and appears innocent by day.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r8.anchor: وذهب ابن عباس ومجاهد إلى معنى مقتضاه: أن «المستخفي والسارب» هو رجل واحد مريب بالليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r9.speaker: الخنساء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r9.claim: Al-Khansāʾ is cited to show that a verbal noun can predicate with an implicit dhāt, “possessing approach and withdrawal”; the poem's lines are omitted in the excerpt.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r10.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r10.claim: Sībawayh rejects interpreting the phrase as “equal among you” without an omitted noun because it begins with an indefinite.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r10.anchor: وضعف هذا سيبويه بأنه ابتداء بنكرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r11.claim: Whether concealed by night or moving by day, both are equally within God's knowledge and encompassing awareness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r11.anchor: سواء في علم الله تعالى وإحاطته بهما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya reads this as one category: the same man makes night his rest and is equally exposed to God's knowledge as the person whose whole conduct is upright.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r12.anchor: فهذا قسم واحد جعل الليل نهار راحته،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r13.claim: The singular traveler is coordinated without repeating man; Ibn ʿAṭiyya says this supports the one-person interpretation because omitting the repeated pronoun otherwise occurs only in poetry.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r13.anchor: ويؤيد هذا التأويل عطف السارب دون تكرار من

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r14.speaker: الأخنس بن شهاب الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r14.claim: Al-Akhnas ibn Shihāb al-Thaʿlabī’s line uses sārin for someone free to move, not restrained or diverted from a direction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r14.anchor: [الأخنس بن شهاب الثعلبي] [الطويل] أرى كل قوم كاربوا قيد محلهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r15.speaker: قيس بن الخطيم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r15.claim: Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm also uses sarabtu in a line as evidence for the sense of moving freely.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r15.anchor: [قيس بن الخطيم] [الكامل] إني سربت وكنت غير سروب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r16.claim: The verse may describe three kinds: a whisperer, its opposite who speaks openly, and a changeable person who sins secretly by night but appears innocent by day; the same analysis extends to deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p299/r16.anchor: وتحتمل الآية أن تتضمن ثلاثة أصناف: فالذي يسر طرف، والذي يجهر طرف مضاد للأول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r1.speaker: قطرب فيما حكى الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r1.claim: Quṭrub, as reported by al-Zajjāj, says mustakhfin can mean apparent, based on an Arabic use of khafaytu for making something visible; an Imruʾ al-Qays line supplies evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r1.anchor: وقال قطرب- فيما حكى الزجاج- مستخف معناه: الظاهر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r2.speaker: قطرب فيما حكى الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r2.claim: Quṭrub, as reported by al-Zajjāj, understands sārin as concealed in a burrow.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r2.anchor: قال: وسارب معناه: متوار في سرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r3.claim: Although Quṭrub's meanings have linguistic support, Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects them because the verse pairs concealment with night and sārin with daytime.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r3.anchor: وهذا القول- وإن كان تعلقه باللغة بينا- فضعيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r4.speaker: امرؤ القيس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r4.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays's line uses khafā for making something apparent, the lexical basis for Quṭrub's reading of mustakhfin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p300/r4.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس: [الطويل] خفاهن من أنفاقهن كأنما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r1.claim: Sārib means someone going along his path or way; the verb is used for traveling through the land.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r1.anchor: ذاهب في سربه بالفتح أي في طريقه ووجهه . يقال : سرب في الأرض سروبا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r2.claim: God knows equally the person hiding in a nighttime refuge and the person traveling openly by day, visible to everyone.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r2.anchor: سواء عنده من استخفى : أي طلب الخفاء في مختبأ بالليل في ظلمته ، ومن يضطرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r3.claim: One parse coordinates “by night and traveling by day” with the full phrase “whoever is hidden.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما أن قوله { باليل وسارب } عطف على من هو مستخف ، لا على مستخف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the conjunction attaches to “hidden,” with min carrying a dual sense, as illustrated by the quoted line about two companions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p486#2/r4.anchor: والثاني أنه عطف على مستخف ؛ إلا أن { من } في معنى الاثنين ، كقوله : نكن مثل من ياذئب يصطحبان

NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r1.claim: Those who speak secretly or aloud, hide at night, or go openly by day are equal in God's knowledge.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r1.anchor: ﴿ سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ﴾ أي في علمه ﴿ ومن هو مستخف بالليل ﴾ متوار ﴿ وسارب بالنهار ﴾

NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r2.claim: Mustakhfin is one who conceals himself; sā rib is one who goes along his way, from saraba in the land, meaning to travel.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r2.anchor: ﴿ ومن هو مستخف بالليل ﴾ متوار ﴿ وسارب بالنهار ﴾ ذاهب في سربه أي في طريقه ووجهه يقال

NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r3.claim: Sārib may coordinate with the full relative clause man huwa mustakhfin, not with mustakhfin alone; alternatively, it coordinates with mustakhfin, with man carrying a dual sense.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p211#4/r3.anchor: سارب عطف على من هو مستخف لا على مستخف أو على مستخف غير أن من في معنى الاثنين

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r1.claim: Secret speech is what a person tells himself, while open speech is what he tells someone else; God knows hidden and public good and evil alike.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r1.anchor: إسرار القول: ما حدث به المرء نفسه، والجهر ما حدث به غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r2.claim: One parsing makes min-kum qualify sawāʾ: the one who speaks secretly and the one who speaks openly are equal among you.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r2.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون وصفا ل«سواء» التقدير: سر من أسر وجهر من جهر سواء منكم

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r3.claim: A second parsing attaches min-kum to sawāʾ with the sense “equal among you,” as in the construction “I passed by Zayd.”
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r3.anchor: على معنى: يستوي منكم، كقولك: مررت بزيد

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r4.claim: A third parsing supplies min-kum separately after both clauses: the one who speaks secretly among you and the one who speaks openly among you.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r4.anchor: على تقدير: سر من أسر منكم وجهر من جهر منكم

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r5.claim: A fourth parsing supplies a deleted noun, meaning that the secret and public speakers are both people of equal standing, like saying Zayd and Amr are just.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r5.anchor: التقدير: ذو سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r6.claim: Another view takes sawāʾ itself as “equal,” requiring no deleted noun.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r6.anchor: وقيل: «سواء» أي مستو، فلا يحتاج إلى تقدير حذف مضاف

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r7.claim: God’s knowledge treats secret and public speech equally, as well as the person hidden in darkness and the one visible on the roads.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r7.anchor: أي يستوي في علم الله السر والجهر

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r8.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash and Qutrub say the night “hidden” person is actually visible: the verb can mean to make something appear or bring it out, as in their cited line by Imruʾ al-Qays.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r8.anchor: الأخفش وقطرب: المستخفي بالليل الظاهر ومنه خفيت الشيء وأخفيته

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r9.speaker: امرؤ القيس
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r9.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s verse is cited as evidence for the sense “made visible” in akhfaytu.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r9.anchor: امرؤ القيس: خفاهن من أنفاقهن كأنما خفاهن ودق من عشي مجلب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r10.claim: Sārib can mean concealed, entering a burrow; the expression is used of a wild animal entering its lair.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r10.anchor: والسارب المتواري، أي الداخل سربا ومنه قولهم: انسرب الوحشي إذا دخل في كناسه

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses mustakhfin as concealed and sārib as visible.

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r12.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r12.claim: Mujahid interprets the hidden person as one concealed in sins and the sārib as one acting openly.

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r13.speaker: الكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r13.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says sārib means one who goes away; saraba, yasrubu, and sarūban mean to depart.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r13.anchor: الكسائي: سرب يسرب سربا وسروبا إذا ذهب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r14.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r14.claim: An anonymous poet’s line about releasing a stallion’s tether witnesses sārib in the sense “going away.”
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r14.anchor: الشاعر: وكل أناس قاربوا قيد فحلهم ونحن خلعنا قيده فهو مسارب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r15.speaker: أبو رجاء
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r15.claim: Abu Raja says sārib is someone going freely over the earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r15.anchor: أبو رجاء: السارب الذاهب على وجهه في الأرض

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r16.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r16.claim: A poetic line is cited for saraba as going or traveling, though its poet is unnamed.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r16.anchor: الشاعر: أنى سربت وكنت غير سروب

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r17.speaker: القتبي
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r17.claim: Al-Qutaybi understands the daytime sārib as quickly going about one’s errands, comparing it to water flowing away.
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r17.anchor: القتبي: «سارب بالنهار» أي منصرف في حوائجه بسرعة من قولهم انسرب الماء

QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r18.speaker: الأصمعي
QURTUBI-FULL:13:10/r18.claim: Al-Asmaʿi explains the expression “leave his sarb” as leave him his way or path.

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.claim: God's complete knowledge, power, and transcendence establish His ability to resurrect, give the signs disbelievers demand, and punish them; He delays these by will according to one group and by wisdom according to another.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r3.anchor: فهذه الآية دالة على كونه تعالى موصوفا بالعلم الكامل والقدرة التامة ، ومنزها عن كل ما لا ينبغي

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.claim: Sawaʾ may be a verbal noun, with an understood 'possessors of equality' as in the example 'Zayd and Amr are just'; or it may mean 'equal' without ellipsis.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r5.anchor: الأول : أن سواء مصدر والمعنى : ذو سواء كما تقول : عدل زيد وعمرو أي ذوا عدل

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.speaker: سيبويه
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.claim: If sawaʾ means mustawin, Sibawayh considers it awkward to begin a sentence with an indefinite active participle.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r6.anchor: إلا أن سيبويه يستقبح أن يقول مستو زيد وعمرو لأن أسماء الفاعلين إذا كانت نكرات لا يبدأ بها

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.claim: A hypothetical respondent prefers the adjective analysis because it avoids supplying an omitted word, which is against the default.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r7.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : بل هذا الوجه أولى لأن حمل الكلام عليه يغني عن التزام الإضمار

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r8.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r8.claim: They gloss sarib as openly moving along one's path; the verse therefore covers a person hidden in darkness and one visible on the roads, both fully known to God.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r8.anchor: قال الفراء والزجاج : ظاهر بالنهار في سربه أي طريقه

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r9.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r9.claim: Al-Azhari illustrates saraba with camels going openly across the land wherever they wish.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r9.anchor: وقال الأزهري : تقول العرب سربت الإبل تسرب سربا ، أي مضت في الأرض ظاهرة

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r10.claim: Whether a person hides in darkness or appears on public roads, God's knowledge encompasses both.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r10.anchor: فمعنى الآية سواء كان الإنسان مستخفيا في الظلمات أو كان ظاهرا في الطرقات ، فعلم الله تعالى محيط بالكل

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse equally covers what hearts conceal and tongues disclose.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : سواء ما أضمرته القلوب وأظهرته الألسنة

RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r12.claim: Mujahid says the verse equally includes people who commit vile acts in the darkness of night and those who do so openly during the day.
RAZI-FULL:v19p14#2/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد : سواء من يقدم على القبائح في ظلمات الليالي ، ومن يأتي بها في النهار الظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r1.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash and Qutrub report the reverse: mukhafi means apparent, while sarib means concealed or hidden away.
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r1.anchor: نقله الواحدي عن الأخفش وقطرب أنه قال : المستخفي الظاهر والسارب المتواري

RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r2.speaker: الأخفش وقطرب
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r2.claim: Their usage is supported by expressions in which khafiya or akhfā means 'made apparent' and ikhtafā means 'extracted'; a grave robber is called mukhtafi, while sarib can describe an animal hidden in its lair.
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r2.anchor: ومنه يقال : خفيت الشيء وأخفيته أي أظهرته

RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r3.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r3.claim: Al-Wahidi judges the reversed definitions sound in Arabic, though Razi prefers the first reading because most exegetes adopt it and night suggests concealment while day suggests visibility.
RAZI-FULL:v19p15/r3.anchor: قال الواحدي : وهذا الوجه صحيح في اللغة ، إلا أن الاختيار هو الوجه الأول

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r1.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ holds that seeking refuge is obligatory before every recitation, inside or outside prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r1.anchor: قال عطاء : الاستعاذة واجبة لكل قراءة سواء كانت في الصلاة أو في غيرها

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r2.speaker: ابن سيرين
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r2.claim: Ibn Sīrīn holds that one recitation of the formula during a lifetime suffices to discharge the obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r2.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين : إذا تعوذ الرجل مرة واحدة في عمره فقد كفى في إسقاط الوجوب

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r3.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r3.claim: The remaining jurists hold that seeking refuge is not obligatory.

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r4.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r4.claim: The majority cite the Prophet's failure to teach the formula among a Bedouin's prayer practices; an objection says that report does not enumerate every prayer obligation, so its silence proves little.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r4.anchor: حجة الجمهور أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يعلم الأعرابي الاستعاذة

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r5.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ argues that the Prophet maintained the practice and that believers are commanded to follow him, supporting its obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r5.anchor: أنه عليه السلام واظب عليه فيكون واجبا لقوله تعالى : ﴿ واتبعوه ﴾

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r6.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r6.claim: He argues that the imperative to seek refuge is obligatory at every recitation, since the ruling recurs whenever its stated cause, reciting Qur'an, recurs.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r6.anchor: احتج عطاء على وجوب الاستعاذة بوجوه

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r7.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r7.claim: He argues that repelling Satan's harm is obligatory, and whatever is necessary to fulfill an obligation is itself obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r7.anchor: ودفع شر الشيطان واجب وما لا يتم الواجب إلا به فهو واجب

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r8.speaker: عطاء
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r8.claim: He also cites precaution as a reason to perform the formula.

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r9.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r9.claim: Most jurists consider seeking refuge recommended before recitation; Mālik omits it in obligatory prayers but uses it in Ramadan night prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r9.anchor: التعوذ مستحب قبل القراءة عند الأكثرين وقال مالك لا يتعوذ في المكتوبة

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r10.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r10.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī reports that Ibn ʿUmar recited the formula quietly and Abū Hurayra aloud, and permits either, though his al-Imlāʾ prefers loud recitation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r10.anchor: روي أن عبد الله بن عمر لما قرأ أسر بالتعوذ وعن أبي هريرة أنه جهر

RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r11.claim: Al-Rāzī reasons that the formula resembles the opening supplication more than al-Fātiḥa, favoring quiet recitation; loudness is a positive quality while quiet is its absence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p58/r11.anchor: المشابهة بينها وبين الافتتاح أتم لكون كل واحد منهما نافلة عند الفقهاء

STUDYQURAN:13:10/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r1.claim: Following 13:9's account of God's all-encompassing knowledge, this verse means He knows everyone's actions whatever their situation.
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r1.anchor: Following directly upon v. 9, which speaks of God’s all-encompassing Knowledge (Bḍ), this verse is understood to mean that no matter what one’s condition is, God is fully aware of one’s actions
