STUDYQURAN:13:10/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r2.claim: Awareness of God's knowledge should produce vigilance in action and constant, intense scrutiny of one's thoughts and heart.
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r2.anchor: This fact is meant to engender not only vigilance in one’s actions

STUDYQURAN:13:10/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r3.speaker: ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r3.claim: The second Caliph ʿUmar is reported to have urged people to take themselves to account before they are held to account.
STUDYQURAN:13:10/r3.anchor: As the second CaliphʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

SULAMI:v1p328#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p328#3/r1.speaker: النصرآباذي
SULAMI:v1p328#3/r1.claim: Whether someone conceals or openly voices what God has entrusted within them, out of concern or joyful love, both remain faithful in the station of wakefulness.
SULAMI:v1p328#3/r1.anchor: قال النصر آباذي : سواء منكم من أسر : ما أودعنا فيه لطائف برنا وكتم إشفاقا عليه ، أو أظهره

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r1.claim: Secret speech and open speech are equal before God; none of His creatures' secrecy or public conduct is hidden from Him.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r1.anchor: معتدل عند الله منكم أيها الناس الذي أسر القول، والذي جهر به،

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r2.claim: The person hidden in night is committing disobedience in its darkness, while the one moving about by day is visible in daylight.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r2.anchor: في ظلمته بمعصية الله {وسارب بالنهار} [الرعد: 10] يقول: وظاهر بالنهار في ضوئه،

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r3.claim: The verb saraba means to appear or come out; Qays ibn al-Khaṭīm's line uses sarabtu for emerging at night despite usually not appearing.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r3.anchor: قال قيس بن الخطيم: [البحر الكامل] أنى سربت وكنت غير سروب … وتقرب الأحلام غير قريب

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r4.speaker: بعض أهل العلم بكلام العرب
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r4.claim: Arab linguists differed over whether the sīn in the expression āmin fī sirbihi is pronounced with fatḥa or kasra.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r4.anchor: واختلف أهل العلم بكلام العرب في السرب فقال بعضهم

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the night figure as a suspicious person hiding, who presents himself by day as innocent of sin.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار} [الرعد: 10] يقول: «هو صاحب ريبة

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the one moving about by day as visible.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r6.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {وسارب بالنهار} [الرعد: 10] : ظاهر

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r7.speaker: أبو رجاء
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r7.claim: Abū Rajāʾ says God knows all of them equally, whether they conceal or disclose speech and whether hidden at night or out by day.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r7.anchor: عن عوف، عن أبي رجاء، في قوله: {سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به، ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار} [الرعد: 10]

TAB-FULL:v13p453/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r8.speaker: أبو رجاء
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r8.claim: Abū Rajāʾ glosses the hidden person as in his house and the daytime figure as going about; God's knowledge of them is the same.
TAB-FULL:v13p453/r8.anchor: عن عوف، عن أبي رجاء: {سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به،

TAB-FULL:v13p455/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r1.claim: Mujāhid says whispering and speaking openly are alike to God; the hidden person is at home and the daytime traveler is abroad wherever he may be.
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: {سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به} [الرعد: 10] يقول:

TAB-FULL:v13p455/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r2.speaker: خصيف
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r2.claim: Khuṣayf says the one hidden at night is recklessly pursuing sins.
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r2.anchor: عن خصيف، في قوله: " {مستخف بالليل} [الرعد: 10] قال: راكب رأسه في المعاصي

TAB-FULL:v13p455/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r3.speaker: خصيف
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r3.claim: Khuṣayf glosses the daytime figure as one who is visible.

TAB-FULL:v13p455/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r4.claim: Qatāda says all these states are alike to God: what is secret is as plain to Him as what is public.
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به} [الرعد: 10] «كل ذلك عنده تبارك وتعالى سواء، السر عنده علانية»

TAB-FULL:v13p455/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses the hidden person as in night's darkness and the daytime traveler as visible.
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r5.anchor: قوله: {ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار} [الرعد: 10] : أي في ظلمة الليل، وسارب: أي ظاهر بالنهار

TAB-FULL:v13p455/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r6.speaker: مجاهد، وعكرمة
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r6.claim: Mujāhid and ʿIkrima both gloss sārib as visible by day.
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r6.anchor: عن خصيف، عن مجاهد، وعكرمة: {وسارب بالنهار} [الرعد: 10] قال: ظاهر بالنهار

TAB-FULL:v13p455/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r7.claim: The first man is nominative as the subject of sawāʾ; the second is coordinated with the first, and the third with the second.
TAB-FULL:v13p455/r7.anchor: من " في قوله: {من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل} [الرعد: 10] رفع الأولى منهن بقوله سواء،

TABRISI:13:8-10/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r1.claim: Because سواء is commonly used, it behaves like an active participle; it may also be nominative as though in the position of مستو.
TABRISI:13:8-10/r1.anchor: أي ذات إقبال وإدبار وهذا مما كثر استعماله أعني سواء

TABRISI:13:8-10/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r2.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:13:8-10/r2.claim: Sibawayh rejects starting with an indefinite active participle, so he would not allow مستو زيد وعمرو.
TABRISI:13:8-10/r2.anchor: إلا أن سيبويه يستقبح ذلك لا يجيز مستو زيد وعمرو

TABRISI:13:8-10/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r13.claim: Those who conceal or voice speech, hide by night, or travel openly by day are alike before God and His knowledge.
TABRISI:13:8-10/r13.anchor: معناه سواء عند الله وفي علمه من أسر القول

TABRISI:13:8-10/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r14.claim: مستخف is one concealed at night; سارب is someone moving along his route and going about his needs by day.

TABRISI:13:8-10/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:13:8-10/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:13:8-10/r15.claim: Sārib is one traveling his route and pursuing his needs by day.
TABRISI:13:8-10/r15.anchor: ومن هو سالك في سربه أي في مذهبه ماض في حوائجه بالنهار

THALABI:v5p273/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p273/r7.claim: Secret and public speech, and one hidden at night and one moving openly by day, are equally known to God.
THALABI:v5p273/r7.anchor: سواء منكم من أسر القول ومن جهر به ومن هو مستخف بالليل في ظلمته وسارب ظاهر بالنهار

THALABI:v5p273/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
THALABI:v5p273/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda explains sārib as one traveling along his path; Qays ibn al-Hatim's line uses sarūb for one who goes along.
THALABI:v5p273/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: سارب بالنهار أي سالك في سربه أي مذهب ووجهة

THALABI:v5p273/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r9.speaker: قيس بن الحطيم
THALABI:v5p273/r9.claim: Qays ibn al-Hatim's line uses sarūb for someone who goes along a path.
THALABI:v5p273/r9.anchor: أي طريقه. قال قيس بن الحطيم:

THALABI:v5p273/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r10.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v5p273/r10.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says sārib means going about one's needs in daytime, from saraba yasrubu.
THALABI:v5p273/r10.anchor: الشعبي: سارب بالنهار منصرف في حوائجه يقال: سرب يسرب

THALABI:v5p273/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r11.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v5p273/r11.claim: The unnamed poet uses sārib for someone gone away.
THALABI:v5p273/r11.anchor: قال الشاعر: أرى كل قوم قاربوا قيد فحلهم … ونحن خلعنا قيده فهو سارب

THALABI:v5p273/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v5p273/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the hidden person to be someone engaged in wrongdoing at night who appears innocent by day.
THALABI:v5p273/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: في هذه الآية هو صاحب ريبة مستخف بالليل، فإذا خرج بالنهار رأى الناس

THALABI:v5p273/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p273/r13.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v5p273/r13.claim: Another view takes mustakhfin as apparent, from khafaytu meaning reveal, and sārib as hidden inside a trail.
THALABI:v5p273/r13.anchor: وقال بعضهم: مستخف بالليل أي ظاهر، من قولهم: خفيت الشيء إذا أظهرته

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r1.claim: Sārib means someone going about his affairs during the day.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r1.anchor: وسارب بالنهار} أي: متصرف في حوائجه. يقال: سرب يسرب.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r2.speaker: الشاعر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r2.claim: An unnamed poet uses sārib for one who has gone away; the line supports the word's sense of going.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p225#3/r2.anchor:
وقال الشاعر:
أرى كل قوم قاربوا قيد فحلهم ... ونحن خلعنا قيده فهو سارب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r1.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r1.claim: Al-Farra and al-Zajjaj analyze nominative sawaʾ with the two clauses that follow; sawaʾ calls for two parties, as in saying Zayd and Amr are equal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r1.anchor: قال الفراء (¬1) والزجاج (¬2): من رفع (سواء) وكذلك الثانية وسواء يطلب اثنين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق وأبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r2.claim: Abu Ishaq and Abu Bakr also allow sawaʾ to mean equal as a participial adjective, without an omitted element; Sibawayh dislikes beginning with an indefinite active participle.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r2.anchor: ذكر هذين الوجهين في (سواء) أبو إسحاق (¬3) وأبو بكر (¬4)، إلا أن أبا بكر يقول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r3.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r3.claim: Abu Bakr prefers sawaʾ meaning equal as the sounder analysis because it avoids ellipsis and uses the overt wording without a pronoun when the meaning remains complete.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r3.anchor: إلا أن أبا بكر يقول: جعل (سواء) بمنزلة مستو أقوى وأصوب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r4.claim: The forms derive through akhfaytu, khafiya, and istakhfa; ikhtafa is also used but rarely, and istakhfa min someone means to hide from them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304/r4.anchor: يقال (¬5): أخفيت الشيء أخفيه إخفاء، فخفي واستخفى، ويقال أيضا: اختفى، وهي قليلة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r1.speaker: الفراء وأبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r1.claim: Al-Farra and Abu Ishaq gloss sari by day as being visible along one's path; sarb means a road or way.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r1.anchor: قال الفراء (¬6)، وأبو إسحاق (¬7): ظاهر # بالنهار في سربه، أي طريقه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r2.speaker: الشاعر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r2.claim: The cited verse says other people tether their stallion while the speaker's tether leaves him free to roam, illustrating sari as moving openly or freely.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r2.anchor: وكل أناس قاربوا قيد فحلهم ... ونحن جعلنا قيده فهو سارب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq says the verse pairs spoken and inwardly concealed words, and people visible on roads with those hidden in darkness: God's knowledge of them is equal.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r3.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق (¬3): معنى الآية: الجاهر بنطقه والمضمر في نفسه، والظاهر في الطرقات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r4.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r4.claim: Abu al-Abbas says the hidden person is concealed and the sari is visible, so the apparent and hidden are alike to God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r4.anchor: وقال أبو العباس (¬5): المستخفي: المستتر، والسار: الظاهر، المعنى: الظاهر والخفي عنده واحد.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says God knows what tongues utter, what hearts conceal, and whoever is concealed by night or visible by day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد علم ما نطقت به الألسنة وما أضمر الفؤاد، ومن هو مستخف بالليل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r6.anchor: ونحو هذا قال قتادة (¬6): سارب ظاهر.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r7.claim: Mujahid says the person hides evil deeds at night and displays them by day; this reading requires supplying sins in both clauses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r7.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬1): مستخف بالليل يعمل السوءات، وسارب بالنهار ويظهرها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi favors the first, general sense, which he says is held by most linguists and exegetes; Abu Bakr argues night implies concealment while daytime suits public visibility.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r8.anchor: هذا الذي ذكرنا في هذه الآية، هو قول أكثر أهل اللغة والتفسير (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r9.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r9.claim: Al-Akhfash reverses the usual senses: mustakhfi is visible and sari is concealed; he cites khafaytu meaning I exposed, as in Imruʾ al-Qays's line.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r9.anchor: وقال الأخفش (¬3): المستخفي الظاهر، والسارب: المتواري، ومن هذا يقال: خفيت الشيء وأخفيته

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r10.speaker: قطرب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r10.claim: Qutrub shares the lexical view that sari is hidden, entering a burrow like a wild animal into its lair; al-Wahidi says this is valid Arabic but prefers the first view for transmitted reports.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r10.anchor: وهذا الوجه مذهب قطرب (¬1) أيضا، وهو صحيح في اللغة غير أن الأول هو الاختيار

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r11.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r11.claim: Abu Bakr supports the common reading because night entails concealment, while openness matches daytime, when people spread out and appear.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p304#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو بكر (¬3): الأول أثبت معنى في الآية؛ لأن الليل يدل على الاستتار

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.claim: Human knowledge is limited, incomplete, and changeable, while God's knowledge is infinite, complete, and certain, including every stage from conception to death.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:13:8/r1.anchor: İnsanların bilgisi sınırlı, eksik ve değişmeye açıktır. Allah’ın ilmi ise sonsuz, tam ve kesindir.

BURHAN:v3p51#2/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p51#2/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p51#2/r1.claim: Hyperbole intensifies an established quality beyond what listeners usually find plausible or mentally possible.
BURHAN:v3p51#2/r1.anchor: المبالغة وهي أن يكون للشيء صفة ثابتة فتزيد في التعريف بمقدار شدته أو ضعفه

BURHAN:v3p51#2/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p51#2/r9.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p51#2/r9.claim: The verse embeds hyperbole in a contrast: knowledge seems inaccessible to human addressees, but is not hyperbolic relative to God.
BURHAN:v3p51#2/r9.anchor: فإن المبالغة في هذه الآية مدمجة في المقابلة

BURHAN:v3p405/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p405/r1.speaker: الأقليشي
BURHAN:v3p405/r1.claim: Al-Uqlishi distinguishes innate perfection in intellect, character, and conduct from excellence achieved through effort and removal of vices; one person has both only figuratively.
BURHAN:v3p405/r1.anchor: قال الأقليشي 2 والحق أنك مهما نظرت إلى شخص

BURHAN:v3p405/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p405/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p405/r5.claim: The explicit equality between secret and public speech clarifies that unseen and witnessed are equal in God's knowledge.
BURHAN:v3p405/r5.anchor: ويوضحه قوله تعالى ﴿ سواء منكم من أسر القول

BURHAN:v3p454/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p454/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p454/r5.claim: Further antitheses contrast concealment at night with appearing by day, and giving dominion with taking it away.
BURHAN:v3p454/r5.anchor: ثم إذا شرط فيهما شرط وجب أن يشترط في ضديهما ضد ذلك الشرط

BURHAN:v3p157/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p157/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p157/r7.claim: A relative pronoun من is understood before سارب and before the clause “none of us but has a station”; the text explicitly gives the parallel phrase about one hidden by night and traveling by day.
BURHAN:v3p157/r7.anchor: وقوله ﴿ ومن هو مستخف بالليل وسارب بالنهار ﴾
